subject.name: NodeRoom note-shaped surfaces, baseline — NoteworthyInbox item list and NotebookDigestWorkbench block list
subject.surface: NoteworthyInbox renders passive room-intelligence entries in a popover list (src/ui/insights/NoteworthyInbox.tsx; src/app/styles.css:220-261). NotebookDigestWorkbench renders notebook blocks in document order in its main column (src/ui/workArtifacts/NotebookDigestWorkbench.tsx; src/ui/workArtifacts/work-artifacts.css:1503-1732).
subject.evidenceRef: source checkout, noderoom worktree at commit 9c99889f (origin/main): src/app/styles.css:224-228 (.r-inbox-list, .r-inbox-item), work-artifacts.css:1598-1632 (.wa-notebook-grid, .wa-notebook-block)

appliesWhenSatisfied: review-in-time-order is the primary job: the inbox lists what the room noticed most-recent-first, and the digest lists notebook blocks in document order
entries are short and heterogeneous: inbox items carry a title, a clamped 3-line preview and metadata; digest blocks are single-paragraph entries with type labels
organization is emergent rather than upfront: inbox items group by detected entity name only when 5+ exist (digest mode), never by user-chosen folders

doesNotApplyWhenChecked.clause: long-form documents with internal heading hierarchy (obs-fabric-contrast/f1)
doesNotApplyWhenChecked.note: Neither surface renders headed long-form documents. Inbox previews are clamped to 3 lines; digest blocks render one paragraph each. The full notebook editor (a Tiptap document) is a different surface and is not scored here.

doesNotApplyWhenChecked.clause: workflows where retrieval at 10k+ items dominates capture (obs-evernote-contrast/f1)
doesNotApplyWhenChecked.note: Both lists are bounded: the digest caps at 48 visible blocks with a '+N more' line, and the inbox collapses into entity digest mode at 5+ items. Neither is a retrieval-at-scale workload.

doesNotApplyWhenChecked.clause: multi-user triage queues where list-vs-detail is load-bearing
doesNotApplyWhenChecked.note: There is no list-vs-detail split to preserve: each inbox item carries its own actions and expansion inline, and digest blocks are terminal (detail lives in the separate editor). No pane pair exists whose separation carries the workflow.

anchors.0: multi-pane chrome with bordered note cards, in the shape of Evernote's three simultaneous panes (obs-evernote-contrast/f1, f2)
anchors.1: one scrolling column, but every entry is a bordered or filled card with its own background and corner radius
anchors.2: mixed treatment: some entries de-carded or the column unified, card chrome remains elsewhere in the entry list
anchors.3: entries separated by dividers only, no per-entry card chrome; residual simultaneous-pane structure remains outside the entry list
anchors.4: a single divider-separated column and nothing else — no cards, no per-note background, no simultaneous second pane (obs-mew-stream/f1)

criteria.question: How are NoteworthyInbox entries bounded — divider or card?

citations.note: Mew separates notes with a 1px rule and nothing else. Every .r-inbox-item ships as a card: background var(--bg-secondary), border-radius 8px, 4px margin between items (styles.css:226).
Per-entry filled cards in a dedicated list is the Evernote list-pane pattern, minus the border. The friction is spent on entry boundaries rather than on reading order.

criteria.finding: Every inbox entry is a filled rounded card. The list is a stack of cards, not a stream. Failed items additionally carry a danger tint and border — that part is state signaling on a trust surface (failed state) and is not counted against this criterion.

criteria.question: How are NotebookDigestWorkbench blocks bounded — divider or card?

citations.note: Each .wa-notebook-block carries border 1px rgba(255,255,255,.065), border-radius 8px, and its own background rgba(255,255,255,.025) (work-artifacts.css:1619-1627). Blocks read as tiles, not as a stream of entries.
Bordered card per note in a list column is the recorded Evernote counterexample shape.

criteria.finding: Blocks are bordered, filled, rounded cards. The needs_review tint (work-artifacts.css:1629-1632) is pending-review state signaling and is retained by design; the uniform card chrome on every block is what falls short.

criteria.question: Does either surface split into simultaneous panes before the entries can be read?

citations.note: Evernote holds three simultaneous panes. The inbox is a single column with zero panes. The digest is a two-column grid (blocks + 28% aside, work-artifacts.css:1598-1603), but the aside is review tooling — patch previews, execution preview, sections — not a second note list or an editor pane.
Mew is one column, full stop. The digest's aside keeps it short of that, though the aside carries proposal/diff trust surfaces that this task explicitly may not fold away.

criteria.finding: Inbox: single column, meets the pane test. Digest: one entry column plus a review aside. The aside hosts trust surfaces (patch previews with before/after diffs) governed by the trust-surfaces contract, so it stays; it is counted here honestly as residual pane structure.

scoreBasis: Ladder: the subject sits at the highest anchor it fully satisfies. c1 and c2 place both entry lists at anchor 1 — one scrolling column whose every entry is a filled card. c3 alone would sit higher but cannot lift a subject whose entry boundaries are cards.
notScored: The full notebook editor (Tiptap document surface) — a long-form headed document, outside this rule per its doesNotApplyWhen.
The wall artifact's capture cards (r-capture-card post-its) — spatial canvas entries, not a time-ordered stream.
Runtime render: scores derive from source and stylesheets at commit 9c99889f; no browser render was measured for this baseline receipt.
Density above the render bounds (48 digest blocks, 5+ inbox digest grouping) — behavior at scale is bounded by code, not observed.
boundary: Scored from the checked-out source, not a running page. Class-to-style mapping was traced by hand from JSX className to stylesheet rules; a computed-style audit could move c1 or c2 if another rule overrides these selectors, but no such override was found in src/app/styles.css or work-artifacts.css.
scoredBy: note-surface corpus scoring pass, noderoom feat/note-surface-dna, against note-surface.stream-not-chrome.rule.json unmodified
